name: O'Reilly Automotive

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (File:O'Reilly Auto Parts Logo.svg)

description: O'Reilly is one of the largest US specialty retailers of car parts, tools and supplies, with 6,585 stores across the US, Puerto Rico, Mexico and Canada at the end of 2025. It sells to two customer groups from the same stores: do-it-yourself car owners and professional repair shops and installers, each about half of sales. Money comes from the markup on parts (gross margin 51.6 percent in 2025) plus same-day delivery to repair shops from a dense store and hub network. It reports one segment. It pays no dividend and returns cash through buybacks ($2.1 billion in 2025).

gics.note: Wikipedia list gives only sector and sub-industry; industry group and industry were not in a source read, so left null.

hq.note: 233 S Patterson Ave, Springfield, MO 65802 (EDGAR business address)

businessLines.name: Sales to professional service provider customers
businessLines.how: Repair shops buy parts on account for each job, delivered the same day; revenue is the parts price on repeat, fragmented customers, and O'Reilly grows it by adding delivery trucks, field sales staff and hub stores.
businessLines.description: Parts delivered same day to independent repair shops and installers from store and hub inventory; includes online ordering via OReillyPro.com

businessLines.name: Sales to do-it-yourself (DIY) customers
businessLines.how: Car owners buy parts and accessories at the counter or online, paid at the point of sale; revenue is price times transactions, helped by the O'Rewards loyalty programme (points are deferred revenue).
businessLines.description: Over-the-counter and online (ship-to-home and in-store pickup) retail sales of parts, accessories, tools and supplies to car owners

businessLines.name: Other sales and sales adjustments
businessLines.how: Wholesale to other parts sellers and staff purchases; the line is net of discounts and rebates so it is not a clean product line.
businessLines.description: Sales to Team Members, wholesale (jobber) sales to other retailers, equipment sales, less discounts, rebates and loyalty-programme deferrals
